transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-10-13 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Oliver Stone (AstraGrid), Priya Rao (AstraGrid), Diego Marquez (AstraGrid)

Summary:
- Intro and mutual context: AstraGrid runs a managed SaaS layer for ISVs and wants a standardized onramp to Redwood for inference routing (hosted + dedicated).
- High level constraints: VPC peering preferred, tenancy isolation, predictable latency (tail < 150ms for 512 tokens), and cost sharing model for burst GPU.
- Agreed next steps: share docs, schedule SE tech deep dive, pilot scope.

Topics covered:
- Onramp patterns (API adapter vs model routing), VPC/private deployment options, billing/revenue share models, security/compliance requirements (SOC2/SSO/RBAC/KMS), sample traffic and perf expectations, pilot timelines.

Action items (captured inline and summarized above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for carving time, um quick round robin - i'm maya, ae for the partners org at redwood, with me is ethan our solutions engineer.
[00:14] Oliver (AstraGrid): hey thanks, i'm oliver, head of cloud partnerships at astragrid, we run a small marketplace and SaaS accel layer for ISVs, excited to chat.
[00:22] Priya (AstraGrid): priya here, solutions architect, i'll be the technical lead from our side.
[00:28] Diego (AstraGrid): diego, vp partnerships, keeping this short.
[00:33] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick note on agenda, want to cover integration patterns, security must-haves, perf profile and pilot scope; call it a framing session.

[01:05] Maya: to start can you give us a bit more on your platform? what are you trying to enable for customers, who are the end users?
[01:17] Oliver: sure - we help mid-market SaaS vendors add LLM features without owning GPU infra; we do auth, routing, tenancy, and take on some observability. customers want predictable costs and enterprise security; many want a managed inference endpoint we can route to either our shared infra or partner backends like redwood.

[02:02] Priya: our model is multi-tenant with per-tenant isolation at the application layer; some larger customers want VPC-to-VPC peering and for us to route inference into their VPCs or to a partner. we also surface billing to the tenant.

[02:28] Maya: got it — so two primary flows: 1) astragrid routes calls to redwood hosted API per-tenant using our routing policy, 2) redwood deploys private/dedicated capacity into an astragrid-managed VPC or a dedicated account — which would be dedicated capacity mode. is that accurate?
[02:49] Priya: yes exactly, though some customers will demand on-prem for compliance; not in scope for first pilot.

[03:10] Ethan: technical clarifiers — what does your traffic look like? tokens per request, QPS peaks, tail latency tolerance?
[03:22] Priya: typical payloads are prompt length 200-600 tokens, 0.5-2 requests per second per tenant on average; peaks up to 80 rps for big tenants. latency SLOs we quote customers are 150-300ms for short completions, but they'd like <150 for interactive features.

[03:55] Ethan: ok that's helpful. for the shared hosted path we can do routing policies and model variants; for dedicated we recommend reserved GPU pools sized to peak QPS. we also have continuous batching and KV caching which helps cost on repeated prefixes.

[04:42] Oliver: can you explain continuous batching? customers are sensitive to tail latency so batching that introduces head-of-line delay is tricky.
[04:55] Ethan: good point — our runtime does adaptive batching: short windows for low latency (micro-batches) and expands when throughput allows; you can configure SLO targets per-route so the router balances cost vs latency. that's why we wanted the traffic profile from you, so we can size batch windows.

[05:38] Priya: security — most of our enterprise customers require SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, keystore, audit logs and sometimes customer-managed KMS. do you support those?
[05:48] Maya: yes — hosted meets SOC2, we have SAML SSO integrations, RBAC at the token/route level, and support KMS integrations for private deployments; for hosted we provide envelope encryption options and audit logs. for the dedicated/private deployments you can bring your own KMS.

[06:22] Diego: what's the controls surface for audit logs? do we get token-level traces?
[06:30] Ethan: we produce per-request metadata, latency and cost breakdowns, and optional request/response logging (configurable retention). for privacy-sensitive tenants you can disable payload logging, but we still surface telemetry for billing.

[07:05] Oliver: ok sounds close. two things: 1) commercial — how would billing/rev-share work if we route to redwood hosted, 2) operational — how do we handle fallbacks when the region is saturated?
[07:20] Maya: commercial is flexible — simplest is reseller model where astragrid bills customers and we invoice astragrid for usage; or revenue share on a per-tenant basis. we can provide pricing tiers for hosted vs dedicated. for fallbacks, our smart routing can route to alternate model variants or regions; can also fall back to lower-cost quantized variants if latency/capacity constraints.

[08:02] Priya: on the network side, peering vs private-link — which do you usually recommend for dedicated?
[08:12] Ethan: peering/VPC peering is common, private link is also supported; we can do transit via interconnects depending on provider. for the pilot we typically recommend VPC peering + strict security groups, and limit ingress by VIPs plus mTLS if needed.

[08:46] Oliver: is there a lightweight integration we can ship quickly to customers to call through astragrid -> redwood hosted while we evaluate dedicated?
[08:56] Maya: yes, npm/python wrappers and a simple API adapter you can embed in your routing layer; we'll share a sample helm chart that proxies tenant tokens and does per-tenant model selection.

[09:20] Diego: benching — will you run a short perf run against our workload to validate tail latency? what's required from our side?
[09:29] Ethan: we need a traffic replay or synthetic harness that approximates interarrival times and token lengths. sample scripts, and ideally a small test tenant we can push traffic against.

[09:48] Priya: we can provide a traffic csv and some GC logs; question — what GPU flavors do you recommend for 70-80 rps peaks for 512 tokens?
[09:58] Ethan: depends on model size; for a 7B quantized variant, a single A10G-ish node often handles a few hundred RPS with batching; for LLama2-70B or higher you'd need multiple H100s and dedicated routing. for pilot we'd recommend starting with a mid-sized open model, sample runs, and tune quantization and batch size.

[10:40] Oliver: do you support multi-architecture images/helm? our ops team wants reproducible infra as code.
[10:47] Ethan: yes — we provide container images and helm charts for private deployment, and terraform modules for VPC and security groups. for hosted there's a light adapter you can deploy. we'll attach a sample repo.

[11:12] Priya: compliance question — if a tenant is in eu, can you guarantee data residency?
[11:20] Maya: yes we have region-specific hosting and private deployments; for EU customers we can pin region and do data residency controls. for strict regulated customers we recommend dedicated or private deployment.

[11:45] Oliver: one risk is mid-pilot if capacity spikes; how do we coordinate escalation?
[11:52] Maya: we'll set up an on-call escalation with SLA for the pilot, and monitoring dashboards; also can enable autoscaling/burst policies.

[12:08] Diego: what's the onboarding timeline? how long to get a pilot live?
[12:15] Ethan: for hosted adapter path we can do a lightweight pilot in 2-3 weeks (adapter + perf run). for dedicated VPC it's 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and network setup.

[12:34] Priya: curious about rollout controls — can we do canary per-tenant and automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated fails?
[12:42] Ethan: yes that pattern is supported. you can set policy: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted, or prefer hosted and overflow to dedicated. we also support A/B and canary percentages per tenant.

[13:06] Oliver: technical nit — how are secrets managed between astragrid and redwood? token exchange?
[13:13] Ethan: typically astragrid holds tenant tokens and proxies requests; for dedicated we support mutual TLS and short-lived signed tokens; for hosted we issue fine-grained API keys and support token scoping.

[13:36] Priya: one of our customers needs FIPS enabled crypto on the path and a BYOK KMS. is that doable?
[13:44] Maya: for private/dedicated yes, BYOK workflows and FIPS are supported; hosted can support envelope encryption with a customer-managed KMS in some cases — we'll check specifics.

[14:05] Diego: any open-source connectors or examples you recommend we look at?
[14:11] Ethan: we have a partner repo with sample adapters for node/python/ruby and a helm chart; also a cookbooks page that walks through peering and private deployments. i'll drop links.

[14:33] Oliver: competitively, we also spoke to orionwave who pitched a lower-cost per-token model but with less observability; curious how you differentiate.
[14:43] Maya: our differentiation is production-grade routing, observability at token level, and predictable economics with batching/caching levers plus fallbacks. we also invest in operator UX and model lifecycle.

[15:05] Priya: on the data plane, how do you handle KV cache eviction per-tenant? we need isolation so one noisy tenant doesn't evict others.
[15:15] Ethan: we shard caches by tenant or route; can set per-tenant cache budgets so noisy tenants can't evict others. that's configurable in the dedicated/private runtime.

[15:42] Oliver: excellent. can you outline the pilot proposal? what minimal success looks like?
[15:49] Maya: pilot scope suggestion: select 1-2 tenants (mix of small and mid), integrate hosted adapter, run 48-72 hour perf tests, measure tail latency and per-token cost, and decide whether to move one tenant to dedicated. success criteria: tail latency <150ms for interactive flows, 20-30% cost improvement with batching/kv caching when moving to dedicated, and no security gaps.

[16:28] Priya: timeline wise we can pick tenants and provide traffic by next week; procurement/compliance review may take 2 weeks.

[16:40] Diego: ok next steps again?
[16:44] Maya: we'll share partner spec, sample helm and adapter repo, and an MOU for a pilot. ethan will schedule the technical deep dive. priya will share traffic profile.

[17:05] Oliver: any blockers on your side?
[17:09] Ethan: nothing major; i just need the traffic synthetics and network contact.

[17:20] Priya: i'll put the traffic csv and infra diagram into the shared folder.

[17:30] Maya: i'll send pricing tiers and reseller options.

[17:38] Diego: sounds good, let's reconvene after the tech deep dive and pilot MOU.

[17:45] (crosstalk)
[17:52] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive and attach docs.
[18:00] Oliver: thanks everyone.

[18:12] -- End of recording --
